chapters.summary: Judita Francis, a mother living in a Volunteers of America shelter, says she has been in the DHS system for 602 days and secured an apartment in April 2026 but still awaits final approval. She describes HRA errors and administrative delays causing anxiety and fatigue.
chapters.title: Judita Francis testifies about 602 days in shelter awaiting CityFHEPS approval

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And the first panel is...

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Jadiah Francis.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Jadita, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Jadita Francis, Akira Morris.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Elizabeth Mackey and Diana Ramos.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And we can start with you and then go down the line.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: Hi.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: Thank you for allowing me to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: My name is Judita Francis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: I've worked over 20 years in the healthcare system, and I've always wanted to help others, which is what brought me here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: At the beginning of this year, I was chosen to be a member of the Client Advisory Board with Volunteers of America, Greater New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: I am also the mother of a brilliant preteen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: Currently, we reside at a Volunteers of America shelter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: I'm sure you are familiar with Volunteers of America Great New York, as they also are a member of FHC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: 601 days ago, that's one year, seven months, and 24 days, I entered the DHS system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: Today is day 602.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: Life happened and I found myself homeless.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: I never thought I'd be in this position.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: After months of living in the shelter, I finally secured a CityFeps shopping letter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: In April of 2026, I was matched to an apartment, but to this day, I am still waiting final approval.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: I am doing everything possible to better our situation, looking for gainful employment, taking care of my child, and handling my end of the application process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: However, the issues with city FEPs are extremely frustrating, and there seems to be no sense of urgency by the three-letter agencies to expedite the process and see it through.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: I have dealt with HRA erroneously removing my child from my public assistance case, placing us in jeopardy of losing everything, including shelter and pending permanent housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: There are many more incidents that have caused anxiety and stress, but time will not permit me to share them all today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: Hearing that I have an apartment should be an exciting moment, but because of the hiccups within the system, it is difficult to feel or display that excitement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: You can continue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: We are given many labels, many negative labels, because we are temporarily housed in shelters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: I and many others are fighting to get rehoused, but the constant errors and delays have left many of us emotionally and mentally fatigued.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: I urge this city and its members to address these issues with urgency, reduce administrative errors and delays, and support all of us who are working diligently to move forward with our lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judita Francis
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: But you could do this.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Akira Morris, a Family Homeless Coalition member, says CityFHEPS helped her move into an apartment but delays at HRA and Homebase almost caused her to lose it. She describes acting as the middleman between her landlord and agencies and urges support for the reforms.
chapters.title: Akira Morris testifies on CityFHEPS delays and near loss of apartment

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: Good afternoon, and thank you for the opportunity to speak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: My name is Akira Morris, and I am a member of the Family Homeless Coalition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: I am here today to speak in support of the bills being introduced to reform city FEPS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: City FEPS is an important program that can make a real difference in the lives of families experiencing housing instability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: I believe these reforms are necessary because they can help families move out of shelter faster, make the process of obtaining a voucher easier, and help families maintain their vouchers once they have them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: I say this not only as an advocate, but also from my own personal experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: After a long and very difficult process, I was finally able to receive a CityFed voucher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: I recently moved into my apartment, and while I am grateful to finally have stable housing, getting there was extremely difficult.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: I experienced housing instability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: And doubling up and came very close to losing the apartment that I worked so hard to secure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: There were significant delays throughout the process, including delays with HRA and Homebase.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: Homebase was backed up with inspections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: There were not enough caseworkers to handle the workload, and there were communication problems between Homebase and HRA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: I was always the middleman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: These delays...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: Had real consequences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: My landlord almost revoked my apartment because the process was taking so long.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: Imagine finally finding an apartment, believing that you are finally on your way out of shelter, and then being at risk of losing that apartment because of administrative delays that are outside of your control.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: Landlords already discriminate families with vouchers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: Families should not have to experience this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: When a family receives a voucher, they should be able to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: Move through the process efficiently and with clear communication and support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: They should not have to constantly worry about losing their apartment because paperwork inspections or communication between agencies were delayed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: These reforms are about more than paperwork.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: They are about helping families.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Finish up.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: I'll keep going.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: They are about helping families get back to their everyday lives and routines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: They are about allowing parents to focus on their children, work, school, and rebuilding their lives instead of constantly worrying about whether they will lose the housing they worked so hard to obtain.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: My experience showed me how important city FEPS can be, but it also showed me where the process can be improved.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: I urge you to support these reforms so that other families do not have to go through the same difficulties I experienced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Akira Morris
utterances.text: Thank you for listening to my story and for considering the experiences of families who are working hard to move from shelter into stable housing.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you for sharing.

chapters.summary: Elizabeth Mackey, a CityFHEPS voucher holder and former ACS worker, says the city failed to pay her landlord for five months and she is now facing court. She asks the council to pass the bills and make DSS and HRA accountable.
chapters.title: Elizabeth Mackey testifies on CityFHEPS payment failure and court threat

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: So my name is Elizabeth Mackey, and I am a member leader with Safety Net, local New York and other organizations throughout the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: So here I am to speak about the needed change with city FEPS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: I have city FEPS, and I used to work for the city for 29 years with ACS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Who am I to say that I was going to be homeless?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Who am I to say I would ever need a voucher?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Who am I to say that I was going to live in an apartment building?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Who was I to say that here I am to testify in front of city council?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Who am I to say I was going to be an advocate?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: To hear, to speak, to work, to do the things that I do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: But here am I to testify again to say City FEPS is a well-needed voucher program that doesn't work for all that is in need of.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: We have so many issues with City FEPS vouchers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: People that waited like I did a year to get an apartment, waited for HRA to cut a check, waited to get an apartment to be expected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: It took months and months for my apartment that I am in that the landlord faithfully waited for me to get the apartment expected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: It took months for a system to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: fell me for the apartment that needed to be expected, but fell twice, but the landlord never gave up on me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: I prayed and prayed for the apartment that I thought that I was going to get, and he prayed with me while a landlord prayed that I would get that apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: But here am I, another part of the process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: The city failed to not pay the landlord five months.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: The landlord wants his money.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Now here I am, going to go to court with the same landlord who prayed for me to get the apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: He's taking me to court.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: So city faps, which I want the bills to get paid to get introduced to, the city failed me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: And one thing that I want the city to do is to do right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: To do right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: And being part of all these organizations and being part of someone who has lived experience and to work here with others who have the same voucher and people that is in these shelters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: All we want is for city council, for all the organizations, and even for the mayor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: To sit back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Have y'all been in shelters?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Do y'all know what it feels like?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Have y'all been to court?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Do y'all know what it feels like?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Maybe not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: But here am I, along with all of these people here,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: They know what it feels like.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: They know what the experience is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: All you have to do is to sign the bills and make people accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Make DSS, HRA, and all these other agencies people to make these bills be passed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: We don't ask for much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: And we should not have to beg, plead for little things that's going to help others to get out of shelter and make permanent housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: These people have children that rely on things that assist them, these systems that we didn't ask for, but they are helpful for us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: So one thing that I'm asking for y'all, do the right thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Sign these bills, but also make DSS, HRA, and all these systems accountable for things that's supposed to do right for the people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Mackey
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Diana Ramos of Safety Net Activists describes moving into an apartment with broken outlets, pests, refrigerator failure, plumbing problems, and mice. She says her transfer voucher is expiring and landlords do not want CityFHEPS because payments are late.
chapters.title: Diana Ramos testifies on uninhabitable CityFHEPS apartment and transfer struggles

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: Thank you for allowing me to speak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: My name is Diana Ramos, and I'm with the Safety Net Activists membership group.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: I had a set testimony going, but thinking about my experience with City FEPS started out with me going into an apartment that looked nice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: But truthfully, no, it's about half of my outlets don't work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: I have pests.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: They had to replace my refrigerator within the first three days of me moving in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: Because a brand new refrigerator wasn't working, I lost $80 worth of food.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: And, you know, that's the inspection process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: But then it's the process of I put in my renewal, I give you my new lease because I renew my city FEPS before I would renew my lease.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: And then finding out that CityFaps wasn't paying the right amount because no one put the new lease amount into being paid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: It was a lot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: Having a call to ask a question, you wait.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: Not knowing, you know, if they got everything they needed for your renewal, you wait.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: You know, there is no data as to how long it takes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: I was not my job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: I was in shelter during COVID.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: So, of course, everything took a little bit longer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: But, you know, people are waiting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: And right now I'm trying to transfer out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: out of that disgusting apartment that I live in because my bathroom barely works.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: And there's just so many issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diana Ramos
utterances.text: And I can't find a place because landlords don't want to take city FEPS because city FEPS is not paying them on time.

chapters.summary: Cathy Batista, Chief Program Officer at Anthos Home, says her organization has helped nearly 1,500 New Yorkers move with vouchers since 2023. She supports Intros 98, 100, 101, and 641, saying vouchers cost far less than shelter but administrative errors and delays block families.
chapters.title: Cathy Batista of Anthos Home testifies in support of CityFHEPS bills

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Hudson and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: I'm Kathy Batista and I'm the Chief Program Officer at Anthos Home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: We help New Yorkers move from shelter into permanent homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: And since 2023, we've helped nearly 1,500 New Yorkers move in with vouchers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: We're also members of the Family Homeless Coalition and support the testimony of the coalition members you heard from earlier today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: Their experience informs our policy requests today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: We strongly support intros 98, 100, 101, and 641.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: Vouchers work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: They are the fiscally responsible choice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: Sheltering a family costs more than $8,100 a month, and a two-bedroom voucher costs $3,058.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: At the same time, vouchers can be very hard to use.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: The state controller found that only 20% of households with a shopping letter get their CityFest voucher approved.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: Too often, administrative difficulties stand between a family and their home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: A complete voucher package can be over 100 pages, and one minor error can send it back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: Voucher holders resubmit and resubmit, and while they wait, documents expire.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: Incomes change, and property providers walk away.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: Property providers also face delays scheduling inspections, re-inspections, over small repairs and late payments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: These bills address just that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: Intro 98 establishes a separate process for resolving minor unit repairs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: Intro 100 requires the city to report how long the process actually takes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: Intro 101 guarantees review and response within 15 days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: And Intro 641 makes sure property providers are paid on time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: We also ask that the city report the most common reasons packages are rejected so we can fix the errors that reoccur.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to comment on these bills, which present logical, impactful, and low-cost changes to the city FEP's process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cathy Batista
utterances.text: We appreciate the committee's consideration and support advancing the bills to the full council.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Jade Vasquez of Win says 97,000 people sleep in city shelters, 70% in families with children, and average family shelter stays rose from 372 to 415 days. She supports Intros 98, 100, and 101 to speed inspections, track lease-up times, and require 15-day processing.
chapters.title: Jade Vasquez of Win testifies on CityFHEPS administrative delays

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Hudson and members of the General Welfare Committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today on these critical CityFEP's administrative reforms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: My name is Jade Vasquez.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: I am the Director of Policy and Research at Wynn, the largest provider of shelter and supportive housing for families with children in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: We operate 16 shelters and 500 units of supportive housing across the five boroughs, and each night 7,000 people call Wynn home, including 3,800 children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: Despite a moderate decline in the shelter census, today 97,000 people sleep in New York City shelters, 70% of whom are families with children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: CityFAPS is our most effective tool to solving this homelessness crisis, but constant administrative delays are keeping families trapped in shelters far longer than necessary.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: For example, the most recent mayor's management report stated that the average length of stay for families in shelter jumped 12% last year, from 372 days to 415 days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: For the 15,000 children under six in DHS shelters, that is nearly a quarter of their lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: And this isn't due to lack of available vouchers, but oftentimes due to city policy, delays caused by city policy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: For example, the administration's new rent reasonableness process has added months to application reviews, causing city FAPS exits and wind shelters to plant by 21% from this time last year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: We thank Speaker Menon and the council for

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: Your leadership on recent investments to CityPhelps expansion and the legislative package being heard today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: We proudly co-crafted some of these bills with direct input from our clients.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: Intro 98 speeds up housing by establishing an inspection hierarchy and allowing minor issues to be fixed on the spot rather than forcing weeks of re-inspection delays.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: Intro 100 mandates transparency by tracking the exact time it takes to secure housing after receiving a voucher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: And Intro 101 establishes predictability by requiring city FEP applications to be processed within 15 days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: CityFaps has proven to work, but it must be modernized and set up for success.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: These bills represent a massive step toward helping our lowest income families find stability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jade Vasquez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Maritza Rico of New Destiny Housing says domestic violence is a leading cause of family homelessness and warns that NYCHA emergency housing vouchers are at risk when funding runs out in November. She supports the bills and calls for a CityFHEPS carve-out for NYCHA EHV households.
chapters.title: Maritza Rico of New Destiny Housing testifies on domestic violence survivors and EHV risk

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair and Councilmember Brewer and Murano for staying.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: My name is Maritza Rico, and I am the Policy and Advocacy Manager at New Destiny Housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: New Destiny is the only organization in New York focused entirely on permanent housing for survivors of domestic violence, which is the leading cause of family homelessness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: We operate the city's first and largest federally funded rapid rehousing program for survivors, and we are the biggest developer and provider of supportive housing for New Yorkers impacted by domestic violence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: As a co-convener of the Family Homelessness Coalition, we support the testimony of the members with lived experience who spoke during the previous panel, their experience and former policy requests.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: We will submit written testimony with our full comments, so I will highlight our main points today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: I must begin by raising the alarm about NYCHA-administered emergency housing vouchers and the thousands of households at risk of losing their homes when funding runs out in November.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Brewer, for meeting with us on this yesterday, and Chair Hudson for your advocacy, your joint letters, and everything else.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: We urge the administration to create a dedicated city FEPS carve-out for NYCHA EHV households, an administrative step that DSS can take now to prevent homelessness and preserve the communities and support networks families have rebuilt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: We deeply appreciate the council's efforts to address CityFEP's administrative burdens through

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: Today's legislation, as we've all said, City of Epsom is critical for the more than 60,000 households, including those survivors with children, especially as the federal funding dwindles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: Our housing navigators work with voucher holders every day and have seen administrative breakdowns cause month-long delays, returns to shelter, and at times return to unsafe housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: We support the intent of the bills, including improvements to inspections, response times, data reporting, and payments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: May I please wrap?

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: Our recommendations are informed by our work inside the system and by survivors'lived experiences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: For instance, response time should account for both DHS and HRA review, and faster processing must not result in more denials.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: We support allowing quick fixes during inspections, but any portal-based improvements will only work if the platform itself is functional and can handle increased volume.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: And while we support faster payments, we are concerned that if lease reviews remain slow, more packages could stall past their leasing dates and require new ones.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: We're happy to be a resource to the council and the committee staff as the bills move forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maritza Rico
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Eric Lee of Volunteers of America Greater New York says CityFHEPS applications can take two to four months and rent reasonableness delays have stretched them further. He supports the bills, suggests 10 business days for responses, and flags HPD registration bottlenecks for small landlords.
chapters.title: Eric Lee of Volunteers of America testifies on CityFHEPS and Homebase delays

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: My name is Eric Lee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: I'm Director of Public Policy for Volunteers of America Greater New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Hudson and members of the committee for allowing me to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: So while these bills aren't being heard today, I do want to flag that VOA supports Intro 232 to shorten housing history requirements for PATH family intake to one year, as well as Intro

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: 816 to allow families to self-attest their housing history at PATH intake.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: By addressing shelter eligibility, these two bills can help also address housing eligibility and streamline access to permanent housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: Currently, our shelter staff report that applications for city fabs can take anywhere from two to four months to be approved.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: They note that since the rent reasonableness test has gone into effect in April, that they've seen delays stretch out to months, and we urge HRA to reconsider the impact of this cost containment measure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: We support the goals of Intro 98 by Councilmember Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: We appreciate the ability for same-day corrections of minor issues there, as well as limited focus re-inspections so that conditions don't continue to churn when they're looking at different reviews.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: We did want to flag that changing the language from assessment to inspection and assessors to inspectors may necessitate additional city funding just so that shelter staff, if they're doing these.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: have building code certification training.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: Let's see, Intro 100, we also support this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: We have some recommendations how to further disaggregate the data by the approval process and different referral and eligibility mechanisms to more closely reflect the experience of the different types of applicants and help outline potential bottlenecks in areas for additional resources.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: We have that in our written, so you can read that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: Intro 101, we also support that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: We just flagged that you may want to change the 15-day to 10-day, 10 business days for consistency's sake.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: And for pre-concerted bill 1424, we support this bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: We wanted to flag that landlords have been messaging to our staff that they are hesitant to take city FEPS because of payment delays.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: One of our survivors recently left our DV shelter, got into permanent housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: And while the three-month advance for city FEPS was paid to the landlord, the ongoing rent never was.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: So now she's worried that her housing is at jeopardy, and we're trying to work with her and the landlord to try to get the issue resolved there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: And I just wanted to also flag Councilmember Banks'intro 1023 related to HPD building registrations that is creating a bottleneck because small landlords are not aware that they need to register with HPD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: Creating an electronic option can help with that bottleneck.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Kelvin Wallace of Anthos Home says he spent 11 months in the shelter system and 7.5 months learning how to apply for CityFHEPS amid changing case managers. He supports Council Member Brewer's 15-day response bill and says the process needs centralized standards and less guesswork.
chapters.title: Kelvin Wallace testifies on 11-month shelter journey and need for 15-day response

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: Good day, Chair Hudson and distinguished members of the City Council Committee on General Welfare.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: My name is Kelvin Wallace.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: I am a program participant at Thantos Home and a founding member of their new initiative, the Speakers Bureau.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: I'd like to share my experience transitioning from a DHS shelter in the Bronx to permanent housing in a vibrant community of Harlem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: I'm here to share my experiences navigating New York City Department of Homeless Shelter System and securing the CityFEP's voucher and finally finding a permanent home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: I'll be testifying in support of Councilmember Gail Brewer's legislation to improve CityFEP's processes, especially voucher response times.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: I've searched for an affordable apartment for months, but my savings ran out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: I got scammed several times during my search.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: I eventually ran out of options.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: Thus began my 11-month journey navigating the New York City shelter system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: I entered on November 17, 2024.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: I was initially told that I would be at the shelter for 90 days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: It seemed as if my particular case didn't warrant extra steps, and I should be able to move through the process quickly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: I'll explain in my written testimony the steps I took before each IOP meeting to be in compliance while still it took many months to obtain my city FEDS voucher while in the shelter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: It felt as if the goalposts for the applications were constantly being moved without any sense of purpose or clarity in the explanation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: It took me seven and a half years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: months living in the shelter trying to do it on my own because my case manager kept changing just to learn how to apply for the city FEPS voucher and have all the required paperwork in hand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: This leads me to emphasize how connecting with Ansel's home became the best thing that could happen to me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: In two short months I was escorted to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: tour three different apartments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: The last one visited became my current residence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: Working alongside the staff at Anthos Home provided me with the help I needed to cut through the overwhelming bureaucracy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: Honestly, I don't know how anyone is expected to handle this process on their own or with very little support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: Clearly, some common sense legislation

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: Reform is needed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: And if nothing else, to have everyone, state, city agency, shelter case workers, and residents who are recipients of the much-needed services all on the same page.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: Council Member Brewer's bill would require Department of Social Services to respond to an application for a city-ship voucher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: Within 15 days after receiving the application, the response would inform the applicant of whether the application has been approved, denied, or requires correction or additional information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: Bottom line, all city FEPS processes should be about the removal of any guesswork, impediments for applying for, receiving, and using the voucher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: I truly believe that a centralized standard, which is applicable across the board, would not only streamline the process, but makes the training.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: transition from homelessness and housing insecurity less traumatizing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: Just the mere fact of being in the shelter system is testimony enough of how urgent housing voucher application reform is greatly needed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: These desperately needed changes to the process would be a dramatic improvement to the current state of uncertainty and apprehension felt by many attempting to navigate the requirements of DHS and the administrative staff at the shelter facility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelvin Wallace
utterances.text: Thank you for allowing me the opportunity to testify before you today.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Hudson calls the next panel of Jean Stevens, Helen Strom, Graham Horn, and Lauren Price. Staff ask whomever would like to begin to go ahead.
chapters.title: Chair Hudson calls panel with Jean Stevens, Helen Strom, Graham Horn, Lauren Price

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Okay, the next panel is Jean Stevens, Helen Strom.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And Lauren Price.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Whomever would like to begin, go ahead.

chapters.summary: Graham Horn of New York Legal Assistance Group says he supports the bills as steps toward improving CityFHEPS administration. He shares a client who submitted three years of renewals and is now $17,000 in arrears while facing eviction, and calls for specific inspection timelines.
chapters.title: Graham Horn of NYLAG testifies in support of CityFHEPS transparency bills

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: Thank you for this opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: My name is Graham Horn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: I'm here from New York Legal Assistance Group.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: I'm honored to stand with and learn from our FHC members who live this reality that some of us work in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: They live it every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: And I am...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: Really grateful that the commissioner is here as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: Our written testimony will follow with more detail, but it is forged in partnership with our shelter and economic stability project and our tenants'rights public housing unit, who have come together to support

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: all of these bills, these intros, as efforts towards improving the administration and effectiveness of city FEPS, as many of the speakers today so far have suggested as

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: first steps or second steps or many in a sequence of never-ending steps that we are excited to continue to be a part of.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: Transparency is deeply needed at all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: levels across the city FEPS system and a client of ours, Miss G, and her young child submitted three years of city FEPS renewals

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: without the subsidy ever changing and now are 17,000 in arrears and facing eviction from a city FEPS funded apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: I was, I was

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: really excited to hear about the October-ish coming of an online platform that will allow

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: participants in the CityFabs program to look and see what's going on, to see if those changes have been accepted or the payments have been issued in the proper amount.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: I think that is deeply needed and a great step forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: A few notes on some of the intros in more detail in the written testimony, but Intro 98, we fully support, ask that it require specific timelines for inspections and re-inspections because that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: interstitial time can be really dangerous.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: Additionally, in eviction prevention cases, housing attorneys are already responsible for the repair section.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: So there should be...

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: We need to start to wrap up.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: Yeah, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: I'll submit it all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Graham Horn
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Helen Strom of the Safety Net Project at the Urban Justice Center says CityFHEPS improvements are sorely needed and rent reasonableness has slowed packets for months. She argues the 15-day timeframe should cover the whole process, including pre-clearance, rent review, and inspections before application submission.
chapters.title: Helen Strom of Safety Net Project testifies on rent reasonableness and pre-application delays

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: My name is Helen Strom, and I'm testifying from Safety Net Project at the Urban Justice Center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: I also support the work of the Safety Net Activists, where our members who have direct experience with homelessness are organizing to get everyone housing in New York City and in the state.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: So on the bills today, I just want to say I think

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: We appreciate the efforts to make improvements to city FEPS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: They're definitely sorely needed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: We also have seen significant slowdowns in people's packets with rent reasonableness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: People whose packets are sold for two, three months and they cannot get them moving because of these rent checks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: We are glad that the city has changed policy on that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: I'll just note the policy changes for rent stabilized apartments and so still yet to be seen whether for people who are trying to get approved for city FEPS with market rate apartments if they are still going to also see delays with the new rent reasonableness policies

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: because it has also been a delay for market rate apartments as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: Intro 100, we're very happy to see a push to speed up application processing times.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: I think one thing we'd like to discuss with the council is there are so many parts of the process that happen before the application is submitted, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: Before you submit an application, you need to do the pre-clearance, you need to do rent reasonableness, you need to do inspections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: All of those things happen before an application.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: can even be submitted for city FEPS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: So we believe the whole process should be taking 15 days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: Like there's months and months and months that are happening of work after someone finds an apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: Like from when you find an apartment to when you're approved, like we want it to get to where that is 15 days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: Like right now people are waiting two or three months before they can even submit an application.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: So, and at one point the agency, a year or two ago, was saying that they were going to review and turn around packets in 48 hours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: Like from when they, so I think our goal would be something that like really captures the whole process because there's so much waiting before you're even allowed to submit your application packet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: And then on intro 100, just.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: Wanting to make sure that we're thinking about all the people who have vouchers who never find or have not found an apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: And how is that getting factored into the average?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: Because the average number of days, that's for people who actually find an apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: But we know that there's thousands and thousands of people with shopping letters sitting in shelters who have not found one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: So making sure we're capturing that too in this data and also capturing why.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Strom
utterances.text: As well.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Jean Stevens of the Benefits Law Project at Volunteers of Legal Service supports Intro 101 and asks the council to extend time limits to Homebase. She says Homebase can take up to 10 months to assemble CityFHEPS-to-stay applications, losing documents and failing to communicate while eviction clocks run.
chapters.title: Jean Stevens of Volunteers of Legal Service testifies on Homebase bottleneck

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: Good morning, Council Members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: My name is Jean Stevens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: I'm the Director of the Benefits Law Project at Volunteers of Legal Service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: Thank you so much for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: Vols strongly supports Introductions 101 because we know that a rapid decision on a CityFAPS application would assist in shielding our clients from eviction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: We also urge the Council to explore other legislation to expedite and streamline, with similar time limitations, the process for applicants applying through Homebase.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: The Benefits Law Project assists New Yorkers who rely on public assistance programs, including CityFAPS, to survive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: With regard to CityFAPS, we work with pro se tenants facing eviction in Manhattan Housing Court to help them resolve their court case and avoid eviction by essentially obtaining rent benefits to pay their arrears so the case is over.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: Generally, there are two types of CityFEP's applications.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: Those who are obtaining CityFEP's to help them move, so they're in shelter or they're being evicted and they need to move and they need CityFEP's to move, and many of my colleagues in testimony today was about that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: Our office, we primarily assist with CityFEP's to stay, so they're getting CityFEP's to help them stay in their current apartment, and that'll get the arrears paid and help them pay their future rent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: We work with veterans, former city shelter residents, and APS recipients.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: They are the people eligible for city FEPS to stay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: In other words, they're very vulnerable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: So what we do is...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: Our office is not able to submit CityFEP's applications itself, so we have to work through Homebase.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: We send our clients to Homebase with incredibly specific instructions of how to seek services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: We then follow up with their Homebase workers by email and phone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: We shepherd them through the intake process, the assessment, the application.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: We check in weekly for updates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: What documents do you need?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: We're working with landlord attorneys in the background to obtain the required landlord documents, and we're having our clients assign their required documents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: Throughout this process, our clients are running against the very short clock in their eviction case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: While we know that Introduction 101 will give a time limit on HRA's application process, we see the major bottleneck is with Homebase.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: It's not uncommon for them to take up to 10 months to put together an application.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: It loses documents, makes repeat Patrick requests, fails to communicate even to us what exactly is needed, doesn't keep tenants sufficiently updated as to what's going on, there's no portal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: They often pivot our clients away from city FEPS into different types of benefits, which will not help them in their court case and will not prevent eviction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: And also, we need to get involved ourselves as attorneys to be like, no, no, no, I'll process them for city FEPS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: To ensure that applicants are approved for city FEPS at a time that would actually prevent their eviction and avoid going into shelter, the council should pass 101 and implement other legislative efforts to streamline the process at the home-based stage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Stevens
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: I was going to say there were many, many nods in agreement.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: We'll have to look into that separately.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Lauren Price of Brooklyn Defender Services supports the bills and says delays at Homebase and rent reasonableness cause clients to lose apartments. She also describes source-of-income discrimination and a pattern of brokers preferring voucher holders with no tenant portion.
chapters.title: Lauren Price of Brooklyn Defender Services testifies on voucher discrimination and delays

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: I'm Lauren Price.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: I'm the Associate Director at Brooklyn Defender Services in our civil practice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: I won't belabor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: You saw me nodding along to everything all my colleagues said.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: We agree on many of these things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: We support all of these bills, and we encourage the council to expand this oversight to the time limit process that everyone else has mentioned about rent reasonableness, about all the delays at home base.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: Our clients...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: Have a common and incredibly frustrating experience, even with advocacy and lawyers and advocates on their side, of signing an apartment when they're desperate to find an apartment,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: going to Homebase to seek out the shopping letter and all the processes to move, and then losing that apartment because it takes so long for everything at Homebase before the packet goes to HRA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: Yes, the time constraints on the HRA packet approval is important, but I agree with what everyone else has said, that it needs to be applied to all the other parts of the preclearance, the rent reasonableness review, and everything else at home base and in the other pre-steps before the application.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: One other part of this process I want to note is that CityFEP doesn't mean that you have

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: Having a voucher doesn't mean you have an apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: And despite...

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: I'm sorry, CityFibs doesn't...

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Can you just pull the microphone a little bit closer?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: Having a shopping letter doesn't mean you will get an apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: And part of that is because we...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: We have strong source of income discrimination laws, but landlords and brokers very much know that enforcement is weak, and they're not likely to be held accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: Non-existent, almost, one might say.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: Also non-existent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: They're absolutely unlikely to be held accountable for turning away voucher holders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: I also want to share that we've experienced a kind of insidious form of voucher discrimination where we've heard that brokers don't want to rent to voucher holders who have a portion of their own.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: So they want to rent only to people whose voucher will be paid, the rent will be entirely paid by the voucher instead of people who work or have Social Security income or other income that would mandate that they have a portion to be paid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: So this discrimination and all other forms of voucher discrimination erode the program and the rights of tenants and people who would be using the vouchers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: The council should work with the commission to enforce source of income discrimination laws and make sure that home-based and shelter staff are equipped to voucher holders to address these.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: And I know the city has increased funding for staff and CHR in this budget, but the level of funding is still very insufficient.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: to allow discrimination to be appropriately investigated in a timely manner, because that needs to be done very quickly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: That's an immediate turnaround, otherwise the apartment will go to somebody else just because of that delay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: Finally, as everyone else has already said, for the program to run efficiently, it's essential that it moves smoothly and quickly at all of the stages.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: There's delays, there's errors, there's lapses in communication.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: And this is all advocates who work with tenants and voucher holders telling you this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: And we are begging the agencies that we work with to work faster.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: People who don't have people on their side sending those emails and calling and following up, I don't know how they ever achieve an apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Price
utterances.text: So we encourage the council to make sure that the appropriate HRA offices and home-based offices are funded, staffed, and trained to meet these guidelines.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you all for your testimony.
